q: Is my company eligible for the SBTi SME target route?
title: Who qualifies for the SBTi SME route?
short: You qualify only if you meet every point of the SBTi's current SME definition: limits on employees, turnover and total assets, independence from any larger group, and not being a financial institution or oil and gas company. Check the exact limits on the SBTi site before applying.

ol: Employees below the SBTi's current SME limit.
Annual turnover below the current limit.
Total assets below the current limit.
Not a subsidiary whose parent group is above these limits. A group decides for its members.
Not a financial institution and not in the oil and gas sector.
Check whether your sector must use a sector-specific route instead, for example if you have land-use (FLAG) emissions.
p: You must meet every point. Failing one sends you to the standard validation route. Take the exact employee, turnover and asset limits from the current SBTi SME definition.

sections.h: What the limits mean in rupees
p: The limits are set in euros. Convert them at the exchange rate the SBTi form asks for, on the date you check, and compare them with your audited figures for the last financial year.

sections.h: What you commit to on the SME route
ul: A predefined near-term target for Scope 1 and 2, in line with 1.5°C. Check the SBTi site for the current target wording, cut and target year.
A commitment to measure and reduce Scope 3, without a numeric Scope 3 target.
Annual public reporting of emissions and progress.
A flat fee that is lower than the standard route; check the current fee schedule.

sections.h: What you need before you apply
ul: A Scope 1 and 2 baseline for the base year, built from fuel invoices and electricity bills.
Your boundary choice under the GHG Protocol, such as operational control, applied to every site.
A first view of your largest Scope 3 categories, since you commit to measuring them.

senseible: Senseible builds the Scope 1 and 2 baseline from your fuel invoices and electricity bills, with the factor and source on every line, which is the core data the SME route needs. It does not submit or validate targets; the SBTi does that.
